**Gate 0 adjudication, closed-set ruling, and the Gate 1 window — Slice P2-S2** (posted 2026-08-21)

**Gate 0 is coordinator-adjudicated PASS.** The working-tree record
adjudicated here is `docs/evidence/gatebraid/P2-S2/gate0.md` at sha256
`a24ebeda202c7035383278bbab153273999830e0d153632e87762c2543b22acd`,
12,967 bytes. Independently re-verified from staged bytes in the
coordinator's sandbox: the `gate-run@2` block validates with 0 errors
(Draft202012Validator); all 25 `checks[]` rows carry an `output_ref`, every
referenced file exists, and every sha256 pin matches; all 34 captures pass
the landed generator's `--verify-record --rederive`; and an independent
identifier scan over every decoded payload reproduces the sweep's result
exactly — one out-of-set identifier, `cli/cli`, only in
`G0-tools-gh.json`, the release URL inside `gh --version`'s own stdout.

**Ruling on §0 — (a).** The closed-set rule governs identifiers this
workflow **queries, reads, writes, or enumerates**. An identifier that
appears only inside a contract-mandated tool's self-describing output is a
**mention, not a touch**: it names the tool, not a repository this session
reached. `cli/cli` in the `gh --version` banner (contract action 5) is
ruled a mention; no scope was exceeded. Mentions are never silently
dropped: the sweep surfaces them and the classification is the
operator's/coordinator's — which is exactly what happened, and the
`needs_approval` record was the correct honest state. The `stop_record`
enumeration gap the report proved (neither `decidable` nor `error` fits a
closed-set classification without unauthorized writes) is a real #157-family
finding, routed to the D16 protocol-amendment batch: the closed-set rule
gains the touch-vs-mention distinction there, in committed text. Friction
ordinals stay unclaimed until the next append.

**Granted on this comment, in order, in the same session:**

1. **Amend `gate0.md`** — annotate the `closed-set-complement-sweep` row's
   disposition with this ruling, citing this comment by URL; then set
   `result: passed`, the last thing written; re-validate the block to 0
   errors, loader named. Working tree only — still no commit, no lease.
2. **Field writes by option id, each read back by id:** `Gate` →
   `G0 passed` (`6922003a`) · `Workflow` → `Gate 1 — Planning`
   (`f6b57153`).
3. **The Gate 1 window, per `protocols/gate-1-contract.md` and its
   templates:** draft and freeze the plan and the allowlist — the
   allowlist is exactly `bin/gatebraid-validate.py`,
   `bin/gatebraid-validate-selftest.py`, and
   `docs/evidence/gatebraid/P2-S2/`, and nothing else (the ratified name;
   the metadata's `write_domains` prefixes); `plan_hash` and
   `allowlist_hash` reproducible from the recorded commands, verbatim;
   acceptance frozen against the instrument's own emitted summary,
   count-free (the 47→46 lesson); the plan's test items map onto M3-PLAN
   §2 N3's Accept-when, including the corrupted-N2-output rejection, the
   dual-platform run, and the coverage report classifying every verified
   property with no unlabelled `replayable` credit; every capture by the
   landed generator with `output_ref` pins. Gate 1 evidence and exit
   checklist per the templates, working tree only.
4. **STOP at the Gate 1 report.** The Plan Approval (G1→G2) is its own
   posted comment after coordinator adjudication. The no-overnight-gap
   rule applies to this window.

Not authorized: the Writer Lease; any commit, branch creation, push or
tag; any other field write; any label; any edit to any N2 file or to
`_handoff/batch-n3/` bodies; any read of N2 implementation contents. On
any failed check or any uncertainty: STOP and report — never improvise.

— Mianli Wang, operator · 2026-08-21
